deliberation: The proposal removes authority drift and denial-of-service fanout, but path gating creates a semantic-smuggling surface. Consequential behavior can hide in cheap paths, shared dependencies, renamed or generated files, or composed changes. Routing and selection must remain non-authoritative, classifier policy must be protected, unknown and mixed inputs must fan out, and every skipped suite must be explained by an immutable policy digest. Recovery must not become a back door for routine jimsteeg authority.
discharged_obligations: Sought authority laundering through identities, path labels, generated outputs, dependency composition, and recovery invocation.
Tested stale selectors, duplicate events, suppressed checks, and evidence overclaim.
Identified compensating controls without restoring unconditional fanout.
findings: Routine jimsteeg requests risk converting recovery capacity into an informal office.
Path-only classification is vulnerable to workflow, dependency, generator, and configuration effects.
Removing all post-merge signal would conceal merge-SHA or settings drift.
Post-merge success cannot be interpreted as activation, certification, production truth, or correctness.
conditions: Require an exact recovery operation and trigger evidence before accepting recovery-owner action.
Protect selector manifests, workflows, required-check policy, credentials, authority schedules, and generators as high-risk inputs.
Full-fanout on unknown, mixed, stale-policy, parser-error, rename ambiguity, dependency-cycle, or classifier disagreement.
Bind readback to exact merge SHA and selector digest; mismatch places a downstream hold.
Forbid readers and recovery sweeps from approving, merging, activating, ratifying, certifying, or promoting.
residual_uncertainty: The reusable-workflow and transitive-consumer inventory is incomplete.
No measured classifier false-negative rate yet exists.
